points.description: States the purpose: both provide broadcasting that is more efficient than flooding, i.e. they minimize the number of duplicate packets in the network.

Reverse Path Forwarding: a node X receiving a packet from sender S via neighbor N checks its unicast routing table and forwards the packet to all adjacent nodes except N only if it would send packets to S via N (assuming the packet arrived on the best route); otherwise it discards it.

Reverse Path Broadcast: nodes monitor unicast traffic to learn which spanning trees/best paths they are part of, and work like RPF but forward only on edges that belong to a spanning tree (excluding the incoming link N).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says it is RPF restricted to tree/selected edges without explaining how nodes learn this from unicast traffic.
